Projects

Motor-driven wearable rehab device

Villanova Capstone · 2024–2025

Requirements

  • < 5 lbs
  • No external tools needed
  • 50th percentile male and female (arm length) users can use it
  • Angle of elbow flexion (0–45 degrees)
  • Gap between fingers and palm when closed < 1 in.
  • Accessible quick power on and off button

Personal responsibilities

  • Created the circuit integrating actuators, Arduino board, power source, buck converter (discarded due to budget and design change), and power switch.
  • Coded a guided user interface (GUI) using Arduino IDE and Processing software.
  • Tested the circuit subsystem, ensuring the power switch works and the power is kept throughout the circuit.
  • Tested GUI and actuator coordination.
  • SolidWorks CAD and design of the hardware encasing.

Results

  • Prototype accomplished and documented for further iterations with a new team.

VESL: Remote Area Community Hotspot for Education and Learning (RACHEL)

VESL — Cambodia, Laos, India · 2022–2023

Requirements

  • Up to 12 devices can connect to the device at a time.
  • Device is charged via a solar panel.
  • Battery storage can be recharged without being fully discharged.
  • Can withstand varying weather conditions.
  • Device can easily be carried from one room to another.

Personal responsibilities

  • Assembled internal battery storage by spot welding multiple lithium-ion battery cells together.
  • Assembled multiple devices.
  • Tested the device using a compressor to ensure the device casing cannot be easily squished.
  • Tested the device using a faucet, finding points in the casing where water can enter.
  • Expanded the number of devices that can access the educational materials on the Raspberry Pi using a TP-Link range extender.

Outcome
